definition: Presumptuous means disrespectfully bold; overstepping one's place.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word presumptuous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know presumptuous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Signing the family's holiday card 'from all of us' struck everyone as presumptuous — he had been dating their cousin for a week.
A forward stranger uses your first name a beat too soon; a presumptuous one has already borrowed your chair.
Shameless goes past presumptuous: the presumptuous guest at least believes he was somehow entitled — the shameless one knows he wasn't and helps himself anyway.

Pushy applies open pressure: the pushy salesman asks again, leans harder, and will not drop it until you give in. Presumptuous skips the pressure entirely — it assumes the yes was already given and simply proceeds. If you felt pushed, the word is pushy; if you were never asked at all, it is presumptuous.

Overfamiliar behavior misjudges closeness: it treats you with a warmth you never licensed, like greeting a near-stranger with a nickname and a shoulder squeeze. Presumptuous misjudges entitlement — your time, space, or credit treated as already granted. The overfamiliar get the tone wrong; the presumptuous take an actual liberty.

After the fire drill, the orchestra resumed the rehearsal without a word from the conductor.
Presumptuous means disrespectfully bold; overstepping one's place.
The newest member of the community garden arrived at dawn with a spade and rearranged three neighbors' plots into what he called 'a more rational layout.' The tomatoes may even have grown better.
It didn't matter: the plots weren't his, nobody had asked, and the presumptuous redesign overstepped far more than the beds he improved.
Presumptuous is the exact word because the offense is the claim, not the manner: he presumed — took as already granted — permissions nobody had given.
He wasn't rude to anyone's face and never raised his voice; a boundary was simply treated as if it weren't there.
That quiet overstep is the whole word.
Presumptuous polices a boundary: someone treated your time, space, or standing as already theirs.

It is about the claim, not the volume — its unit-mate insolent is loud disrespect flung up at authority, while the presumptuous colleague may be perfectly pleasant right up until you notice your parking spot is gone.
If no line was crossed and the only error is a swollen self-estimate, the plainer word is overconfident.

Two weeks after joining the band, Theo announced our summer schedule.
He had booked four weekend shows, accepted a festival slot in July, and given the organizers our names — all without asking a single one of us.
When Maya objected that she worked weekends, Theo looked genuinely surprised.
It had not occurred to him that the yes was ours to give.
That was the presumptuous part: not the ambition, which we shared, but the way our time was treated as something already granted to him.
We played the July festival in the end.
Theo, we voted, would handle the posters and ask first next time.
